set.body:
Phase 2 replaced the divergent unweighted summation with trapezoid quadrature (Quadrature.boxOffsets), so the box response now converges and matches R evaluate.HRF exactly. That closed the correctness gap.

The remaining win is accuracy and speed: several families have a closed-form antiderivative, so the box response could be an exact difference of primitives rather than a quadrature sum.

- gamma / SPMG: incomplete gamma
- FIR / tent / B-spline: exact piecewise polynomial
- everything else: keep the trapezoid fallback

This also removes the O(h) convergence floor that the discontinuous kernels currently have (see HrfLaws.quadratureConvergence, which had to be stated as a refinement rate rather than a fixed tolerance precisely because of this).

Shape suggested by the tractatus section 6.3: integration as a capability rather than a method every kernel pretends to implement exactly. Fits the existing HrfDescriptor dispatch pattern already used by DerivativePolicy and PenaltyPolicy.

Context: docs/plans/hrf-hardening.md sections 5 and 7.
set.title: RFE: exact analytic primitives for box-response integration
